articles.title: From Market Stalls to Kitchen Tables: How Global Turmoil Is Hiking Mexico's Food Bills
articles.summary: A 66-year-old retiree in Monterrey still buys tomatoes and chiles, but the prices sting. Global fuel and fertilizer costs, plus highway crime, are driving Mexico's food inflation to 8.1%—hitting low-income families who spend 70% of income on food.

articles.title: UK Braces for Record-Breaking Heatwave: 30.5°C and Rising
articles.summary: Saturday hit 30.5°C in Kent, the year's hottest day, and temperatures could soar to 33°C on Monday—potentially breaking a May record from 1944. Amber heat alerts warn of health risks, while climate change fuels the early-season scorcher.

articles.title: Tulsi Gabbard Resigns as Intelligence Chief Amid Husband's Cancer Battle and Policy Clashes
articles.summary: DNI Tulsi Gabbard stepped down to care for her husband with rare bone cancer, but her tenure was marked by controversy: she appeared at an FBI raid on Georgia election offices and opposed the Iran war, reportedly clashing with Trump's inner circle.
